CHAPTER ONE
A Bell in the Orchard

At first light, Mira counted the glass trees from the eastern gate. Their
branches held yesterday's rain in bright, trembling beads. Beyond the hedge,
the old bell waited beneath a canvas hood.

"You heard it too?" Jalen asked.

Mira nodded. The bell had rung once before dawn, although no rope hung from
its bronze mouth. She drew the map from her coat and marked a small circle at
the edge of the orchard. The mark was only a test; it was not a promise.

***

They crossed the wet grass slowly. Each step made the nearest branches chime,
and the sound moved outward in a widening ring. A blue moth settled on
Jalen's sleeve, folded its wings, and became still.

At the orchard's center, a seam of warm air opened between two trees. Mira
could see another sky through it—amber, cloudless, and full of distant birds.
She reached for Jalen's hand before the seam could close.
